newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan defence agency plans cuts in budget--paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan defence agency plans cuts in budget--paper.

text.p: Japan's Defence Agency is planning major cuts in spending on weapons systems from its five-year budget plan that extends to the end of March 2001, a Japanese daily reported on Thursday, citing agency sources.

The mass-circulation Yomiuri Shimbun said the cutbacks would be on frontal weapons systems such as tanks, escort ships and F-2 fighters and cover Japan's ground, air and maritime Self-Defence Forces (SDF).
The paper said the agency also plans to reduce the amount of money it spends to support U.S. military forces in Japan as well as reducing the budget for SDF logistical support.
The Defence Agency declined to comment on the article, but a spokesman did say the agency would release a budget request plan at the end of August.

According to the Yomiuri, among the major items that will be cut are the purchase of 47 F-2 fighters at 12 billion yen ($100 million) per plane and eight escort ships at 63 billion yen ($529 million) each. Tanks and other weapons systems for the Ground Self-Defence Force, or army, would also be subject to the cuts, the paper said.

It said the agency's plan was in line with a government scheme to cut 920 billion yen ($7.73 billion) from the 22.15 trillion yen ($186 billion) defence budget plan for five years to fiscal March 31, 2001.

The amount of money the agency requests for frontline military hardware in its budget for this fiscal year would likely be cut by six to seven percent from the original 841 billion yen ($7.06 billion) request, the paper said.
It said the agency would also increase its purchases from the private sector of items such as trucks that it used to order through exclusive contract arrangements.

The paper did not give details on the planned size of the cutback in financial support to U.S. forces in Japan. The latest figures available from the defence agency show that for fiscal 1996 it set aside 273.5 billion yen ($2.30 billion) from its budget as its contribution to the cost of the U.S. presence that year.
The United States has about 47,000 military personnel stationed in Japan.
